added_failures_note: unmeasured: the reviewed manifest names no base gate log, so the added-failure count was not taken

findings.text: - _run_head_for_review now delegates to _review_head_and_tree, so for a reclaimed worktree whose record names no head it returns the repository head where it previously returned the empty string; its two remaining callers, _review_dispatch_fields (recovery.py:435, which composes the dispatch head and grants the head-keyed write path) and _failed_review_backend (recovery.py:1207, the dropped-lane comparison), both change behaviour on that edge, neither is covered by any test, and neither the manifest nor the commit body names them.

- once the worktree is reclaimed _review_head_and_tree passes tree=None, so select_review_for_head cannot reconstruct a legacy record naming no revision and returns the newest stored record without checking the revision it describes (recovery.py:322); this is more permissive than base, which refused it by reconstructing against the shared checkout — accepted here as policy, but a legacy record of a different revision can now stand as this run's evidence.

item_verdicts.goal: the dispatched goal was to repair the two findings the review of a8422de3 left open against recovery._stored_review; recovery.py:576 now resolves both the head and the reconstruction tree through one helper (_review_head_and_tree, recovery.py:1098), so a reclaimed worktree pairs the record-carried head with no reconstruction tree and a record naming no head falls back to the repository head rather than the empty string that selected the newest stored record whatever revision it described.
item_verdicts.manifest: its commits (08a8a7d2f7, 94b56333f), changed_paths, tests and negative_control_log match the tree; logs/gate-rereview-lane.log reads 12 passed EXIT=0 and logs/negative-control-red.log ends 2 failed EXIT=1; it names its gate only under test_logs and no baseline_suite/after_suite, so the crew reader's added-failure derivation reads unmeasured against this manifest.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the grant is recovery.py, the test file, an evidence fragment and a figures directory; the two commits touch exactly reckon/crew/recovery.py, tests/test_rereview_keeps_its_lane.py and the evidence fragment, and the figures directory is correctly left unused.

justifications.durability: the two new checks are isolated (isolated_project fixture under tmp_path) and each reddens against the reverted module, so a regression that re-merges head and tree, or restores the empty-head fallback, fails; deducted because the change also folds _run_head_for_review onto the same helper, and that altered edge (worktree reclaimed and record naming no head) is exercised for neither of its remaining callers, _review_dispatch_fields and _failed_review_backend, which no test covers on that path, and because a legacy record with no revision is now accepted as the newest without any check on the revision it describes.
justifications.evidence: both arms reproduced here to the node's own counts — head arm at 94b56333, 12 passed EXIT=0 over the focused file; base arm with recovery.py at a8422de3, 2 failed / 10 passed EXIT=1, the two new checks red at base and green at head so they discriminate — and adjacent tests that exercise the changed helper pass 11 at head; deducted because the reviewed manifest names no baseline_suite/after_suite so the standard added-failure derivation reads unmeasured rather than zero, and the delivered gate log's revision line names 08a8a7d2 while the delivered head is 94b56333 (the head adds only the evidence fragment, so the gate measured the production commit).
justifications.fit: the repair reuses the existing helpers and adds one small private function (_review_head_and_tree) rather than a second head-resolution path, and it removes the duplicated resolution that let _stored_review pair a record-carried head with the shared checkout; no new symbol is exported and no plan identifier appears; deducted because folding _run_head_for_review onto the new helper changes two callers' behaviour on an edge outside the two findings, so the change reaches slightly beyond what it repairs.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the repair does exactly what the two findings ask — _stored_review resolves head and reconstruction tree through one helper so the two can no longer come from different sources, a reclaimed worktree's recorded head is paired with no tree so a legacy record is not reconstructed against the shared checkout, and a record naming no head falls back to the repository head rather than the empty string; the live-worktree path and the record-carried-head path are unchanged, and both new checks reproduce their finding's failure at the parent module and pass at head.
justifications.scope_discipline: three changed paths, all inside the grant; both commits carry a conventional subject and a body with no AI trailer and no plan or sprint identifier; the change adds no ruff finding (head 6, base 6 across the same two files) and the format finding on recovery.py is pre-existing (base reports one too); no plan state, index or peer path is touched.
